name: Assegno Unico Universale - SIA Project 24 25
description: The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. The system validates fiscal codes, handles ISEE information, calculates payments, and allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications. Suspended applications may require additional documents. Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.
rawDescription: The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. The system validates fiscal codes, handles ISEE information, calculates payments, and allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications. Suspended applications may require additional documents. Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.
highLevelGoals: To successfully apply for the Assegno Unico Universale benefit for their dependent children.
To have the flexibility to create, save, resume, and update their AUU benefit applications at their convenience.
To access comprehensive information about the AUU benefit and estimate potential allowance amounts.
To track the progress and status of their submitted AUU benefit applications.
To effectively review, approve, reject, or suspend AUU applications to ensure timely benefit decisions.
To verify the validity of applicant data and ensure correct benefit calculations according to regulations.
To handle applications requiring additional documentation or special attention.
To contribute to and finalize an AUU application initiated by another parent.
To modify how the AUU benefit is distributed among eligible parties.
lowLevelGoals: Applicant sends a request to the system to start a new AUU benefit application.
Applicant inputs and submits their personal identification details (e.g., tax code, name, surname) to the system for the application.
Applicant inputs and submits the required details for each dependent child (e.g., name, date of birth, tax code) to the system.
Applicant inputs or links their ISEE declaration details to the application in the system.
Applicant selects and submits their preferred method for receiving the benefit (e.g., bank transfer, postal order) to the system.
Applicant requests and views a comprehensive summary of all entered application data before final submission.
Applicant sends a request to the system to formally submit their completed AUU benefit application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to save the current state of an incomplete AUU application as a draft.
Applicant sends a request to the system to retrieve and load a previously saved draft of an AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to modify data within a specific section of a draft AUU application.
Applicant inputs and submits details for a new dependent child to be added to an existing (draft or submitted) AUU application.
Applicant uploads specific additional documents to the system in response to a request for more information for a suspended AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to permanently remove a saved draft of an AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to access general descriptive information about the AUU benefit.
Applicant inputs specific family income and composition data into the system to calculate an estimated benefit amount.
Applicant sends a request to the system to display the calculated estimated AUU allowance amount based on provided data.
Applicant sends a request to the system to access detailed rules and conditions for AUU benefit eligibility.
Applicant sends a request to the system to fetch a list of all AUU applications they have previously submitted.
Applicant sends a request to the system to display the current processing status of a particular submitted AUU application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to fetch any notifications or alerts related to their submitted application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to download official documents or communications pertaining to their application.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to fetch a list of all AUU applications awaiting review.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to display all details of a specific AUU application.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to mark a specific AUU application as approved.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to mark a specific AUU application as rejected, providing a mandatory reason.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to suspend a specific AUU application, triggering a request for additional information from the applicant.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to reassign a specific AUU application to another INPS employee for processing.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to verify the applicant's identity against external national databases.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to verify the details of dependent children against external national databases.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to fetch the official ISEE declaration data for an applicant from the relevant national database.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to initiate an automatic calculation of the AUU benefit amount based on verified application data.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to flag an application for manual review due to detected data discrepancies or inconsistencies.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to formally ask an applicant for specific additional documents for their application.
INPS Employee uploads supplementary documents received from an applicant or other sources to a specific application in the system.
INPS Employee adds internal, private notes or comments to an application for tracking special attention or context.
INPS Employee sends a request to the system to mark an application's exception status as resolved after all issues have been addressed.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to accept an invitation to collaborate on an existing AUU application initiated by another parent.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to view the details of an AUU application shared with them for collaboration.
Co-parent inputs and submits their personal identification details for the shared application.
Co-parent uploads any documents specifically required from them for the shared application.
Co-parent inputs and submits modifications or completes missing sections within an AUU application shared with them for collaboration.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to confirm their completion and submission of their part of the shared application.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to propose a specific percentage for how the AUU benefit should be distributed.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to view the currently proposed or agreed-upon distribution of the AUU benefit.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to confirm their agreement to the proposed benefit distribution.
Co-parent sends a request to the system to modify the payment method for their specific share of the AUU benefit.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are accurate and cover the main user roles described in the text: the primary applicant, the INPS staff for administrative processing, and the co-parent who can modify or complete applications. There are no obvious omissions or contradictions.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are well-aligned with the system description and actors. They correctly capture the functional needs of the Applicant (applying, managing drafts, understanding benefits, monitoring status), the INPS Employee (processing, compliance, handling exceptions), and the Co-parent (collaborating, modifying distribution). There are no non-functional goals (like security or performance) included, which is correct per the instruction to ensure ONLY functional goals are present. The goals are representative of the core functionalities described.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are comprehensive and well-aligned with the high-level goals and the software description. They correctly capture the functional actions for all three actors (Applicant, INPS Employee, Co-parent). The goals are specific, atomic, and functional. There are no obvious contradictions or major omissions regarding the core functionalities described (application creation, management, processing, collaboration, and simulation). The inclusion of specific actions like "Trigger Automatic Benefit Calculation" and "Verify Applicant Identity" appropriately addresses the system's validation and calculation requirements.

branch_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Applicant Successfully Submits AUU Benefit Application
branch_001.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process an applicant undertakes to prepare, review, and formally submit an application for an AUU benefit. They cover all necessary steps from initiating the application and providing various required details (personal, dependent, financial, payment method) to reviewing the compiled information and finally submitting the application to the system.

branch_002.rationale: These low-level goals collectively describe the comprehensive set of actions an applicant can perform to create, modify, save, retrieve, and delete their AUU application, including adding details and documents, throughout its lifecycle from initial draft to post-submission updates. They all pertain to the applicant's direct interaction and control over the application's content and state.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Add Dependent Child to Existing Application
Upload Additional Documents for Suspended Application

branch_003.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Applicant to evaluate potential AUU benefit
branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively enable an applicant to gather comprehensive information about the AUU benefit, understand its eligibility criteria, and calculate a personalized estimated allowance. This integrated set of operations supports the applicant in assessing their potential entitlement and the financial implications of the benefit.

branch_004.rationale: These low-level goals collectively enable an applicant to comprehensively monitor and stay informed about the status, progress, and related communications for all their previously submitted AUU applications. They cover retrieving a list of applications, checking individual application status, receiving alerts, and accessing official documents, all of which are essential for tracking.

branch_005.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the necessary actions for an INPS Employee to effectively process AUU applications. This includes retrieving lists, viewing details, making approval or rejection decisions, suspending applications for further information, and reassigning them, all of which are integral steps in the application processing workflow.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Suspend AUU Application for More Information

branch_006.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the actions an INPS Employee performs to gather, verify, and utilize applicant data from various national databases to calculate the AUU benefit amount, including flagging applications for manual review when discrepancies are found. These operations are all integral steps in the comprehensive processing and initial assessment of an application for the AUU benefit.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Retrieve ISEE Data from National Database

branch_007.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the actions an INPS employee takes to address incomplete applications or those with identified issues. This involves requesting and uploading necessary additional information, adding internal notes for context or special attention, and ultimately resolving any outstanding exceptions or deficiencies to progress the application.

branch_008.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Co-parent Collaborates on Shared AUU Application
branch_008.rationale: The low-level goals describe a complete workflow for a co-parent to engage with an AUU application initiated by another parent. This includes accepting an invitation, viewing details, providing personal information and documents, making necessary modifications, and finally confirming their contribution to the shared application. All these actions are integral steps for a co-parent to effectively collaborate on and complete their portion of a shared application.

branch_009.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Manage AUU Benefit Distribution and Payment Arrangements
branch_009.rationale: These operations collectively enable co-parents to propose, view, agree upon, and subsequently manage the practical payment methods for their respective shares of the AUU benefit. They cover the full lifecycle from establishing the distribution to managing its execution.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Request Change to Co-parent Payment Method

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is a valid, high-level stakeholder intention. However, the hierarchy is fragmented. The sibling HLG 'Manage Application Progress' covers the creation, saving, and updating of the application, while 'Monitor Application Status' covers post-submission tracking. The original HLG focuses on the final act of submission and the overall success of the application process. In Goal-Oriented Requirements Engineering, the end-to-end process of applying (creating, filling, submitting) is often treated as a single high-level goal or a tightly coupled set. Here, 'Manage Application Progress' and 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' are distinct phases of the same primary workflow: the former is the preparation/drafting phase, the latter is the finalization/submission phase. While they are distinct, 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is slightly ambiguous ('Secure' can imply security or obtaining). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant Successfully Submits AUU Benefit Application' is more precise. However, looking at the other goals, 'Manage Application Progress' is about the *process* of managing the draft. 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is the *outcome* of that process. Is it redundant? No, because one is about the flexibility of the draft state, the other is about the successful completion. Is it fragmented? Yes, but they represent different states. However, a better consolidation would be to have one HLG for 'Apply for AUU Benefit' which encompasses both managing progress and submitting. Since 'Manage Application Progress' exists, and 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' exists, they are somewhat overlapping in scope regarding the 'application' artifact. But 'Manage Application Progress' explicitly mentions 'create, save, resume, update', while 'Secure' implies the final 'submit'. Given the rubric, if a broader sibling entails the original, remove it. 'Manage Application Progress' does not entail submission. 'Monitor Application Status' is post-submission. Therefore, 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' is a distinct, supported goal representing the finalization of the application. It is not a mere workflow step of 'Manage Application Progress' because submission is a state change that ends the 'progress' phase and begins the 'status' phase. It is a valid independent HLG. The name 'Secure' is slightly weak but acceptable in the context of 'securing a benefit'. The reconstruction is clearer. I will keep the original as it is supported and distinct from the siblings, though a rewrite to 'Submit AUU Benefit Application' might be better, the current one is not materially defective enough to require a rewrite under strict criteria unless 'Secure' is considered misleading. 'Secure' is a common term for 'obtain'. I will keep it. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs cover the core data entry steps (identification, children, ISEE, payment) and the final submission. However, the project description explicitly states that applicants must 'accept declarations and privacy notices' as part of the application process. This is a mandatory legal step for 'successfully applying' that is absent from the current LLGs. Additionally, the description mentions specifying 'custody' information, which is a distinct data category from general child details or household info, and is not explicitly covered by llg_003 (which focuses on child details) or llg_002 (applicant ID). While 'household' might be inferred, 'custody' is specific to the AUU context (shared custody affects allowance calculation/distribution) and is explicitly listed in the description ('specify child, household, custody and payment information'). The absence of the declaration/privacy acceptance step is a material omission for a 'secure' and compliant application.

Keeping 'Efficient Application Processing' as a separate HLG alongside 'Ensure Application Compliance' and 'Manage Application Exceptions' fragments the employee's primary duty. The most appropriate action is to rewrite the broadest suitable goal to serve as the umbrella. Since 'Efficient Application Processing' is the core action (deciding on the application), it is the best candidate to be rewritten into the umbrella goal 'Process AUU Applications', which would then encompass the compliance checks and exception handling as sub-goals or related aspects, or alternatively, the hierarchy should be consolidated. replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. The system validates fiscal codes, handles ISEE information, calculates payments, and allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications. Suspended applications may require additional documents. Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.

Rewrite the functional intention for actor 'INPS Employee' using this focus: Rewrite to 'Process AUU Applications' to serve as the umbrella goal for reviewing, validating, deciding (accept/reject/suspend), and managing exceptions for AUU applications.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description explicitly states that a co-parent can 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information'. The current HLG 'Collaborative Application Management' is defined as 'To contribute to and finalize an AUU application initiated by another parent'. This HLG semantically entails the outcome of completing the application, which includes the necessary steps to modify distribution information as part of finalizing the collaborative submission. The separate HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' was previously evaluated and recommended for removal as a fragment of the broader collaborative management outcome. No other actor-level functional requirements are left uncovered; Applicant and INPS Employee responsibilities are fully covered by their respective HLGs.

branch_004.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Monitor Application Status' is supported by the description ('consult submitted applications'). However, the hierarchy is fragmented. 'Manage Application Progress' covers the pre-submission lifecycle (create, save, resume, update), while 'Monitor Application Status' covers the post-submission lifecycle (track progress/status). Together, they form a single end-to-end stakeholder intention: managing the entire lifecycle of an AUU application from initiation to final status. Neither goal is a strict subset of the other, but they are phases of the same workflow. According to the consolidation audit, if the hierarchy is fragmented and no sibling is yet a valid umbrella, the broadest suitable goal should be rewritten to become that umbrella. 'Manage Application Progress' is the broader term that can encompass both the active management (pre-submission) and the monitoring (post-submission) of the application. Therefore, 'Monitor Application Status' should be removed, and 'Manage Application Progress' should be rewritten to cover the full lifecycle. Since I am evaluating 'Monitor Application Status', and it is a fragment of a broader intention that is better expressed by a sibling, and the sibling is not yet an umbrella, the correct action for this specific fragment in a bottom-up consolidation where we are looking for independent outcomes is to recognize it as a workflow phase. However, the prompt asks to decide for the *original* HLG. If I keep it, the fragmentation remains. If I remove it, I must ensure the intention is captured elsewhere. The instruction says: 'If the hierarchy is fragmented and no sibling is yet a valid umbrella, choose REWRITE for the broadest suitable goal so it can become that umbrella.' This implies I should rewrite the *broadest* goal. But I am evaluating 'Monitor Application Status'. Is it the broadest? No. 'Manage Application Progress' is broader. So, should I remove 'Monitor Application Status' and rewrite 'Manage Application Progress'? The decision options are for the *current* HLG. If I choose REMOVE, I am saying this intention is covered by another HLG or is unsupported. It is not fully covered by 'Manage Application Progress' as currently defined (which focuses on create/save/resume). It is not unsupported. It is a fragment. The rubric says: 'A supported but materially over-fragmented goal must receive score 0-2 and a corrective decision, not KEEP.' The corrective decision for a fragment that should be merged into a sibling is typically REMOVE (if the sibling is rewritten to cover it) or REWRITE (if this one is the one to be expanded). Since 'Manage Application Progress' is the more natural umbrella term, 'Monitor Application Status' is the fragment to be absorbed. Therefore, REMOVE is the appropriate decision for this specific HLG, with the understanding that 'Manage Application Progress' will need to be rewritten in its own evaluation to cover the full lifecycle. Alternatively, if I must pick one to rewrite, 'Manage Application Progress' is the better candidate. But I am evaluating 'Monitor Application Status'. Removing it acknowledges it is a sub-goal of the broader 'Manage Application Progress' intention.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description outlines three main actor groups: Applicants, INPS Employees, and Co-parents. 

1. **Applicant**: Capabilities include creating/saving/resuming applications (covered by 'Manage Application Progress'), submitting/accepting declarations (covered by 'Secure AUU Benefit Application'), adding children (covered by 'Manage Application Progress' or 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' as part of the application lifecycle), consulting submitted applications (covered by 'Monitor Application Status'), accessing general info (covered by 'Understand Benefit Information'), and simulating allowance (covered by 'Understand Benefit Information').

2. **INPS Employee**: Capabilities include accepting, rejecting, or suspending applications (covered by 'Process AUU Applications'), handling suspended applications requiring additional documents (covered by 'Manage Application Exceptions'), and validating data/calculations (covered by 'Ensure Application Compliance and Accuracy'). The retired HLG 'Efficient Application Processing' is fully subsumed by 'Process AUU Applications' and 'Ensure Application Compliance and Accuracy'.

3. **Co-parent**: Capabilities include completing an existing application (covered by 'Collaborative Application Management') and modifying allowance distribution (covered by 'Flexible Allowance Distribution').

All explicit functional requirements are entailed by the current HLGs. No distinct actor-level outcomes are missing.

The original HLG 'Process AUU Applications' accurately captures the end-to-end functional outcome for the INPS Employee actor. The project description explicitly states that INPS employees can 'accept, reject or suspend applications' and that 'suspended applications may require additional documents' (implying exception management). The bottom-up reconstruction confirms this scope. This goal is distinct from the Applicant and Co-parent goals, which focus on creating, managing, or understanding the application from the user side. There is no broader sibling goal for the INPS Employee that would make this redundant, nor is it a fragmented phase of a larger unstated goal; it represents the complete processing lifecycle for the employee. The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. Authenticated applicants can create applications, specify child, household, custody and payment information, save drafts, resume applications, accept declarations and privacy notices, and submit applications. The system validates fiscal codes, handles ISEE information, calculates payments, and allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications. Suspended applications may require additional documents. Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information. Applicants can also add children to existing applications, consult submitted applications, access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS_FOUND. The project description explicitly states that 'Authenticated applicants can create applications... save drafts, resume applications... and submit applications.' The current HLG list for the Applicant actor only covers 'Understand Benefit Information' (consultation/simulation) and 'Update Existing Application with New Dependents' (modifying a submitted application). There is no current HLG that covers the primary workflow of creating a new application, managing its draft state (saving/resuming), and submitting it for the first time. The retired HLG 'Secure AUU Benefit Application' or 'Manage Application Progress' previously covered this, but it is not entailed by the current HLGs. 'Update Existing Application' is distinct from 'Create and Submit New Application' as the former implies a prior submission and specific modification of dependents, while the latter is the initial lifecycle entry point including draft management.

missing_goal_requests.generation_project_description: Generate an HLG for creating, drafting, and submitting new AUU applications. branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Understand Benefit Information' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information, and simulate the expected monthly allowance.' This represents a distinct stakeholder outcome (pre-application assessment/consultation) separate from the transactional workflows of creating a new application ('Manage New Benefit Application') or modifying an existing one ('Update Existing Application with New Dependents'). The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant assesses potential AUU benefit entitlement' accurately captures the intent of accessing information and simulating allowance to evaluate eligibility. The goal is appropriately scoped, not redundant with other Applicant HLGs, and aligns with the documented capabilities. Therefore, it should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Understand Benefit Information' is supported by the project description which states applicants can 'access general AUU information' and 'simulate the expected monthly allowance'. The current LLGs decompose this into retrieving general info (llg_001), inputting data for estimation (llg_002), viewing the estimate (llg_003), and retrieving eligibility criteria (llg_004). While 'simulate' implies inputting data and viewing results, 'access general AUU information' is broad enough to encompass eligibility criteria as part of understanding the benefit. All LLGs are directly entailed by the documented capabilities of accessing information and simulating allowance. There are no unsupported LLGs (e.g., no notifications or downloads) and no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG and documentation. The decomposition is precise and consistent.

branch_003.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Process AUU Applications' is fully supported by the project description, which states that INPS employees can 'accept, reject or suspend applications' and that 'Suspended applications may require additional documents.' This represents a distinct, end-to-end stakeholder outcome for the INPS Employee actor, separate from the Applicant and Co-parent goals. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage the Review and Decision Process for AUU Applications' is semantically equivalent to the original goal, capturing the same scope of reviewing, validating, deciding, and managing exceptions. There are no other HLGs for the INPS Employee that would make this redundant, and it is not a fragment of a broader goal. The granularity is appropriate for a high-level goal representing the core operational workflow for this actor. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Process AUU Applications' is supported by the documentation stating INPS employees can 'accept, reject or suspend applications' and that 'Suspended applications may require additional documents.' However, the current LLGs include several capabilities that are not explicitly stated or necessarily entailed by the documentation. Specifically, 'InitiateAUUApplicationValidation' (llg_003) and 'ViewAUUApplicationValidationResults' (llg_004) imply an automated validation workflow that is not described; the documentation only mentions the system validates fiscal codes/ISEE (likely at submission) and that employees make decisions. 'RecordSuspensionReason' (llg_008) is a specific data entry action not explicitly required by 'suspend applications'. 'UpdateSuspendedApplicationStatus' (llg_010) is a generic status update that overlaps with the decision actions (Accept/Reject) and is not explicitly documented as a distinct 'update status' operation separate from the final decision. While retrieving pending/suspended applications (llg_001, llg_009) and viewing details (llg_002) are necessary preconditions for processing, the inclusion of unsupported validation and specific recording actions constitutes a material defect. The essential capabilities are the decisions (Accept, Reject, Suspend) and managing the exception (handling additional documents for suspended cases), which are partially covered but mixed with unsupported steps.

branch_004.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Complete Shared Application Data' is supported by the documentation, which states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application'. The goal correctly identifies the actor (Co-parent) and the specific outcome (providing personal, child, household, and custody information to finalize the application). It is distinct from the sibling HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution', which focuses specifically on modifying how the benefit is distributed, whereas this HLG focuses on the completion of the application data itself. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Co-parent to complete their contribution to a shared AUU application' is semantically equivalent to the original but slightly less descriptive regarding the types of data involved. The original goal is well-scoped, supported, and not redundant with other HLGs. It represents a distinct stakeholder outcome (finalizing the co-parent's part of the application) separate from just modifying distribution rules. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the parent HLG 'Complete Shared Application Data'. The documentation states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application'. The LLGs cover the necessary steps: retrieving the application state (llg_001), submitting the specific data categories mentioned in the parent description (personal, child, household, custody - llg_002 to llg_005), and finalizing the contribution (llg_006). These capabilities are explicitly supported by the project description which lists 'child, household, custody and payment information' as part of the application process, and the specific actor capability to 'complete an existing application'. There are no unsupported LLGs (e.g., no notification or download features added) and no essential capabilities are missing for this specific scope (payment information is typically handled by the primary applicant or is part of the general application setup, but the parent HLG specifically highlights personal, child, household, and custody info for the co-parent's contribution; even if payment were included, the current set is not contradictory, but strictly speaking, the parent description lists 'personal, child, household, and custody information'. The LLGs align perfectly with this list. The 'Finalize' step is a necessary entailment of 'completing' the data. The sibling HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' handles the modification of distribution, which is distinct from completing the base data. Therefore, the decomposition is valid and supported.

branch_005.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Update Existing Application with New Dependents' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states: 'Applicants can also add children to existing applications'. This represents a distinct stakeholder outcome from creating a new application ('Manage New Benefit Application') or understanding benefit information. It is not a mere workflow phase of another goal but a specific capability to modify an existing record to reflect changes in family composition. The bottom-up reconstruction aligns with this intention. The goal is appropriately scoped and does not overlap with the Co-parent's goals, which focus on completing shared data or modifying distribution, rather than adding new dependents to an applicant's own record. Therefore, the goal should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the parent HLG 'Update Existing Application with New Dependents'. LLG 001 (Retrieve) is necessary to identify and load the existing application for modification. LLG 002 (Add new dependent) directly addresses the core capability of adding children to an existing application, which is explicitly supported by the project description ('Applicants can also add children to existing applications'). LLG 003 (Submit updated application) is necessary to finalize the changes, as the system requires submission to officially update the record. There are no unsupported LLGs, and no essential capabilities are missing. The decomposition is precise and aligned with the documentation.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS_FOUND. The project description explicitly states that 'Applicants can also... consult submitted applications'. The current HLG 'Manage New Benefit Application' covers the creation and submission of new applications, and 'Update Existing Application with New Dependents' covers adding children. However, neither HLG semantically entails the capability to view, review, or consult the status and details of previously submitted applications. The retired HLG 'Monitor Application Status' covered this outcome, but its deletion left a gap because no current HLG addresses the applicant's need to access information about their existing, submitted applications.

branch_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Understand Benefit Information' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information' and 'simulate the expected monthly allowance'. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Applicant to evaluate potential AUU benefit' accurately captures the intent of these capabilities. This goal is distinct from 'Manage New Benefit Application' (which focuses on the transactional process of creating and submitting an application) and 'Consult Submitted Applications' (which focuses on reviewing existing records). Understanding the benefit and simulating the allowance are pre-application or informational activities that constitute an independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome, separate from the act of applying. Therefore, the goal is appropriately scoped and should be kept. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current LLGs accurately decompose the parent HLG 'Understand Benefit Information'. The project description explicitly states that applicants can 'access general AUU information' (supported by llg_001 and llg_004) and 'simulate the expected monthly allowance' (supported by llg_002 and llg_003). The inclusion of 'Retrieve Detailed Eligibility Criteria' (llg_004) is a reasonable and necessary entailment of 'access general AUU information' and 'comprehensive information' in the context of understanding benefit eligibility, as eligibility rules are core informational content for such benefits. No capabilities are unsupported, and no essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG and documentation are missing. The decomposition is precise and aligned with the provided description.

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' is supported by the project description, which states that a co-parent can 'modify allowance distribution information'. However, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage AUU Benefit Distribution and Payment Arrangements' is more precise and comprehensive, as it captures both the distribution and the associated payment arrangements implied by the management of such benefits. The original name is slightly vague ('Flexible' is not explicitly in the text, though 'modify' implies flexibility). More importantly, looking at the hierarchy, the Co-parent has another HLG 'Complete Shared Application Data'. The description says the co-parent can 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information'. These are two distinct capabilities: providing missing data to finalize the application vs. modifying how the money is split/paid. They are not strictly the same workflow phase; one is about data completion, the other about financial arrangement. Therefore, they are independently satisfiable outcomes. The original HLG is valid but could be better aligned with the reconstruction's clarity. However, 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' is a reasonable high-level name for 'modifying allowance distribution information'. The reconstruction adds 'Payment Arrangements' which might be slightly broader than just 'distribution information', but distribution often entails payment methods. Given the options, KEEP is appropriate as the original goal is supported and distinct from the sibling 'Complete Shared Application Data'. The name 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' is acceptable for 'modify allowance distribution information'. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description states that a co-parent can 'modify allowance distribution information'. It does not describe a multi-step negotiation workflow involving 'proposing' percentages, 'viewing proposals', or 'confirming agreements' (llg_001, llg_002, llg_003). These specific interaction patterns are not entailed by the text, which simply states the ability to modify the information. Furthermore, llg_004 ('Request Change to Co-parent Payment Method') is partially supported as payment information is part of the application data, but the specific framing of 'requesting a change' as a distinct workflow from 'modifying distribution information' is not explicitly detailed. More critically, the description says the co-parent can 'complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information'. The current LLGs focus heavily on a hypothetical negotiation process (propose/view/confirm) that is not in the documentation. The documentation supports a simpler capability: modifying the distribution details (percentages and potentially payment methods associated with those shares) directly. The specific LLGs llg_001, llg_002, and llg_003 introduce unsupported workflow steps (proposal/confirmation cycle). llg_004 is also slightly off because 'payment method' is generally part of the application data, but 'modifying allowance distribution information' is the explicit capability. The decomposition invents a complex state machine for distribution that is not documented. The essential capability is simply to modify the distribution information (percentages and associated payment details) for the co-parent's share.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. All explicit functional requirements from the project description are covered by the current High-Level Goals. The Applicant's capabilities to create, save, resume, and submit new applications are covered by 'Manage New Benefit Application'. The ability to add children to existing applications is covered by 'Update Existing Application with New Dependents'. The ability to consult submitted applications is covered by 'Consult Submitted Applications'. Accessing general information and simulating allowances is covered by 'Understand Benefit Information'. The INPS Employee's responsibilities to accept, reject, suspend applications, and manage exceptions (additional documents) are covered by 'Process AUU Applications'. The Co-parent's responsibilities to complete shared application data and modify allowance distribution are covered by 'Complete Shared Application Data' and 'Flexible Allowance Distribution'. No explicit functional requirements remain uncovered.

branch_002.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete set of actions an INPS Employee needs to perform to manage the lifecycle of AUU applications. This includes retrieving applications for review, accessing detailed information, initiating and viewing validation results, and making final decisions (accept, reject) or interim status changes (suspend, update suspended applications). All operations are focused on moving an AUU application through its processing workflow.

branch_007.rationale: Both low-level goals empower the Co-parent to control different aspects of the AUU benefit's distribution: one concerns the allocation percentage among eligible parties, and the other concerns the payment method for their own allocated share. Together, they represent the Co-parent's ability to manage how the benefit is divided and received.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Update Payment Method for Co-parent Share

branch_002.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The High-Level Goal 'Process AUU Applications' accurately captures the end-to-end functional outcome for the INPS Employee actor. The project description explicitly states that the system 'allows INPS employees to accept, reject or suspend applications' and that 'Suspended applications may require additional documents'. The bottom-up reconstruction confirms that the Low-Level Goals cover the complete lifecycle management for this actor, including reviewing, validating, making decisions, and managing exceptions. This goal is distinct from the Applicant and Co-parent goals, which focus on creating, updating, or consulting applications. It is not a fragment of a broader goal, nor is it redundant with other HLGs, as it is the only HLG assigned to the INPS Employee. The scope and granularity are appropriate for a stakeholder outcome. Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Process AUU Applications' for the INPS Employee. The project description explicitly states that INPS employees can 'accept, reject or suspend applications' and that 'Suspended applications may require additional documents'. The LLGs cover the necessary workflow: retrieving pending and suspended applications (llg_001, llg_009), viewing details (llg_002), initiating and viewing validation (llg_003, llg_004), and making decisions to accept (llg_005), reject (llg_006), or suspend (llg_007) applications. The inclusion of recording suspension reasons (llg_008) and updating suspended application status (llg_010) is supported by the requirement to manage exceptions and handle additional documents for suspended cases. No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are unsupported or misleading.

branch_007.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original High-Level Goal 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' is supported by the project description, which states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' The bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage Co-parent's AUU Benefit Distribution' aligns with this intention. The goal is distinct from 'Complete Shared Application Data' (which focuses on providing personal/household data to finalize the application) and 'Process AUU Applications' (INPS employee). It represents a specific, independently satisfiable stakeholder outcome for the Co-parent: controlling how the benefit is allocated and received. The granularity is appropriate for a High-Level Goal, as it encapsulates the management of distribution percentages and payment methods without being overly fragmented or redundant with other Co-parent goals. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' is defined as modifying how the AUU benefit is distributed among eligible parties. The project description explicitly states that 'Another parent can complete an existing application and modify allowance distribution information.' The current LLGs cover the two primary aspects of this distribution: the allocation percentages (llg_001) and the payment method for the co-parent's share (llg_002). Both are directly supported by the documentation's mention of modifying 'allowance distribution information' and the general context of specifying 'payment information' in applications. There are no essential capabilities missing from the parent goal's scope, and no LLGs are unsupported or misleading. The decomposition is precise and complete for the stated goal.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for NO_MISSING_HIGH_LEVEL_GOALS. The project description outlines capabilities for Applicants (create/submit, consult, add dependents, understand info/simulate), INPS Employees (process/decide, handle suspensions/documents), and Co-parents (complete shared data, modify distribution). All these functional requirements are semantically entailed by the current High-Level Goals: 'Manage New Benefit Application', 'Consult Submitted Applications', 'Update Existing Application with New Dependents', and 'Understand Benefit Information' cover the Applicant; 'Process AUU Applications' covers the INPS Employee (including suspension and document handling as part of processing); and 'Complete Shared Application Data' and 'Flexible Allowance Distribution' cover the Co-parent. No explicit actor-level functional requirement is left uncovered.
